sources.title: Introducing Claude Opus 5
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The July 24 launch names Opus 4.8 as predecessor and describes Opus 5 as approaching Fable 5 capability. It gives no total/active parameter count or size-preserving relationship to a named, sized base; performance and price comparisons do not establish parameter lineage.

sources.title: Claude Opus 5 - Claude Platform Docs
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. Exact-model specifications retain 1M-token context, adaptive thinking, text/image inputs and text output, and July 24 release. Its current-lineup comparison table has context, output, price, thinking, effort and knowledge-cutoff columns, with no total or activated-parameter column.

sources.title: System Card: Claude Opus 5
sources.evidence: Fresh official PDF retrieved October 27, 2026 at 10:18:51 UTC; independently inspected its extracted text. Section 1, page 11 describes Opus 5 pretraining followed by post-training/fine-tuning, without naming a separately sized base. The executive summary calls it an upgrade to Opus 4.8. Table 8.1.A on pages 152-153 compares benchmark results. Full-text parameter/size/lineage searches found no nominal total or active parameter count; effort parameters are inference settings.

sources.title: System Card: Claude Opus 5.5
sources.evidence: Fresh official PDF retrieved October 27, 2026 at 10:11:48 UTC and independently inspected. Table 8.1.A, page 174, compares Opus 5.5, Opus 5, Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra benchmark results, with no total or activated-parameter row/column. Training text and full-text parameter/size searches give no nominal Opus 5 count; an upgrade relationship does not identify a sized base.

sources.title: System Card: Claude Fable 5.1 & Claude Mythos 5.1
sources.evidence: Fresh official PDF retrieved October 27, 2026 at 10:18:48 UTC and independently inspected. Table 8.1.A, pages 167-168, includes an Opus 5 benchmark column, with no total or activated-parameter counts. Training and full-text parameter/size searches do not establish an Opus 5 size or a shared sized base.

sources.title: System Card: Claude Sonnet 5.5
sources.evidence: Fresh official PDF retrieved October 27, 2026 at 10:11:47 UTC and independently inspected. Table 8.1.A, page 109, reports benchmark scores for Sonnet 5.5, Sonnet 5, Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Sol, rather than model sizes. Other Opus 5 references and full-text parameter/size searches supply no Opus 5 total or active count.

sources.title: System Card: Claude Haiku 5.5
sources.evidence: Fresh official PDF retrieved October 27, 2026 at 10:11:48 UTC and independently inspected. Table 8.1.A, page 111, compares Haiku 5.5, Haiku 4.5, Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6 Luna benchmark results. Other Opus 5 references and full-text parameter/size searches contain no nominal Opus 5 total or active parameter count.

sources.title: GLM-5.3 and the spread of advanced cyber capabilities
sources.evidence: September 29, 2026 article evaluates Opus 5 and explicitly states Claude models cannot be abliterated because their weights are not publicly released or customizable. Used solely as distribution evidence.

sources.title: Commercial Terms of Service
sources.evidence: Terms govern Anthropic API use, grant permission to use hosted services, restrict reverse engineering/duplication, and reserve intellectual-property rights except as expressly granted. Supports proprietary service classification, not an open-weight license.

sources.title: PDF support - Claude Platform Docs
sources.evidence: All active models support PDF processing; each PDF page is converted to an image and accompanied by extracted text. Combined with Opus 5 active status and vision support, supports the catalog PDF input format.

sources.title: Prompting Claude Opus 5
sources.evidence: Exact-model guide describes complex agentic coding and enterprise work, a 1M default/maximum context, tool calling, and default-on thinking. It explicitly discusses structured tool_use blocks.

sources.title: Anthropic Transparency Hub - Claude Opus 5 Summary Table
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. Exact Opus 5 summary identifies pretraining followed by post-training and describes text/image understanding with text output. Its architecture/training heading supplies no nominal parameter count, active count, structural architecture or named sized base.

sources.title: Claude Opus 5 - AI BENCHY model facts
sources.evidence: Inspected October 27, 2026 as a numeric lead only. Labels approximately 5T total and 500B active as an external industry estimate and links its Parameter source to the April 9 NextBigFuture article (s14). That linked article identifies no Opus 5 checkpoint and supplies no 500B active figure; these are not developer specifications.

sources.title: Anthropic and xAI Model Parameter Counts
sources.evidence: Inspected October 27, 2026 to resolve the AI BENCHY source chain. The April 9, 2026 article attributes a 5T Opus figure to Elon Musk and links his April 9 post. It refers to unspecified then-current Opus, predates the July 24 Opus 5 release, and gives neither Opus 5 attribution nor a 500B active count. It cannot support transfer of a nominal size to this record.

sources.title: Estimating the Parameter Counts of the Claude 5 and GPT-5.6 Families
sources.evidence: Inspected October 27, 2026 as an independent measurement lead. Its corrected Opus 5 figure is 2.1T IKP-effective parameters, a knowledge-capacity proxy explicitly distinguished from true weight count; it gives a 609B-7.2T interval before additional imputation uncertainty. It explicitly concludes that its data supports no Fable 5/Opus 5 lineage conclusion. It supplies no developer nominal size or active count.

sources.title: Claude Opus 5 Trillion Parameters: Evidence Review of the 5T MoE Claim
sources.evidence: Inspected October 27, 2026 as a numeric lead only. The page labels 5T total and 500B-1T active as unconfirmed reports/estimates and relies on inferred MoE ratios, cost/throughput reasoning and an alleged Musk remark. Its assertion that Opus 5 was unannounced is stale against the official July 24 launch. No Anthropic source on the page establishes these counts.

name.note: Exact public and API model name.

developer.note: Official announcement and exact-model system card identify Anthropic as developer.

family.note: System card identifies the model as Opus-class; catalog family normalization is appropriate.

release_date.note: Announcement says available today and is dated July 24, 2026; exact-model specification independently lists that release day.

open_weights.note: Explicit general Claude distribution statement applies to Opus 5, which the same article evaluates; API availability alone was not used as proof.

license.note: Descriptive proprietary classification for a hosted, nonpublic-weight model under Anthropic commercial terms; no open-weight license claimed.

parameters_b.note: October 27 re-audit found no nominal total count in the reopened exact-model card, launch, documentation, transparency entry or four later cards. The Opus 4.8 predecessor/upgrade wording does not identify a sized base. Fresh exact-name searches for parameter count, billion/trillion parameters, base model, same weights, 5T and 500B resolved the 5T rumor to an April statement about unspecified Opus and the 2.1T result to an expressly nonliteral knowledge-capacity proxy. Neither supplies a developer nominal count or size-preserving lineage inference; null is not based on requiring a tensor census.

active_parameters_b.note: Rechecked independently of total size. Current model documentation and the exact/later cards have capability, price and inference-setting comparisons, with no nominal active/activated-parameter disclosure for Opus 5. The 500B and 500B-1T leads are third-party MoE estimates; the linked April article supplies no active count, and the IKP study measures knowledge capacity rather than active computation. No architecture or equality with total parameters is assumed.

architecture.note: Reviewed exact-model training text and later cards do not disclose structural architecture. Targeted Anthropic and Transformer Circuits interpretability/training searches did not locate exact Opus 5 evidence; no Transformer or MoE inference is made from other Claude models or general frontier-model claims.

context_window.note: Exact-model documentation gives 1M tokens as both default and maximum context.

modalities.note: Text/image input and text output are exact-model specifications. PDF is a supported document input processed into text and page images, not a separate native sensory modality.

reasoning.note: Adaptive thinking is supported and enabled by default; it can be disabled at effort high or below.

tool_call.note: Exact-model guide documents tool calling and structured tool_use blocks.

description.value: Claude Opus model for complex agentic coding and enterprise work, with adaptive thinking and a 1M-token context window.
description.note: Replaces the stale strongest-Opus superlative with stable supported capabilities; later Opus 5.5 has superseded this model.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit preserves both counts as undisclosed after reopening the exact card, release, current overview and transparency entry, and independently checking four later official cards and their comparison tables. Fresh numeric and named-base searches resolved the 5T/500B lead to an unsupported transfer from an April statement about unspecified Opus, and the 2.1T lead to a knowledge-capacity proxy that expressly cannot establish true size or lineage. No developer nominal count or explicit size-preserving lineage from a sized base was found. All other field assessments are preserved.
